chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar Al-Sabaty, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who has a young wife, and she menstruates every two months or three months with one menstruation. How should her husband divorce her? He said: Her matter is difficult. She is divorced with a divorce of the Sunnah, with one pronouncement, upon purity, from without sexual intercourse, with witnesses. Then she is left alone until she menstruates three times, whenever she menstruates. So when she has menstruated three times, her waiting period has ended.

It was said to him: And if a year passes and she has not menstruated three times therein? He said: When a year passes and she has not menstruated three times, she is observed for three months after the year, then her waiting period has ended.
It was said: If he dies or she dies? He said: Whichever of the two dies, the other inherits, for the period between it and fifteen months.
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period (Iddah) calculated for a woman with irregular menstruation who does not menstruate regularly?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific legal procedure for a woman with irregular menstruation (al-ha’id al-mustahaddah), establishing that her waiting period (Iddah) is determined by three actual menstruations rather than a fixed calendar duration. The Imam clarifies that if three menstruations do not occur within a year, an additional three months are added, ensuring the Iddah is complete even in cases of prolonged amenorrhea. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of adapting legal timelines to biological reality while maintaining the sanctity of the marital bond during the transition.
